title: Post-earnings drift on the announcement-return surprise
hypothesis: Stocks in the top fraction of the 3-session abnormal return around their results date outperform the point-in-time NIFTY 500 (with a liquidity floor) over the next 20 to 60 sessions, after delivery charges.

mechanism.text: Investors under-react to earnings news; arbitrage is limited in less liquid names.

evidence.source: Bernard and Thomas, Journal of Accounting Research 27
evidence.finding: Prices drift for about 60 days after earnings surprises.

evidence.source: Chordia, Goyal, Sadka, Sadka and Shivakumar, Financial Analysts Journal 65(4)
evidence.finding: Drift concentrated in illiquid stocks; costs eat most of it.

evidence.source: Event study of 469 Indian firms (University of Nottingham eprint 26569)
evidence.finding: Drift for bad news over about a week; good news priced fast.

evidence.source: Post-earnings drift in NSE firms, Trends Economics and Management
evidence.finding: Drift present after surprises, into the third month.

universe.name: nifty500-pit-liquid
universe.rule: NIFTY 500 members on the results date with a 60-session median traded value of at least ₹10 crore.

turnover.basis: capital cycling about 6 times a year x 0.33% CNC round trip

prior_trials.basis: No event rule has been run in this repo.

holdout_rule.pass_if: Holdout mean abnormal return of the selected events above zero after charges, over at least 100 events.

kill_criteria: Holdout mean abnormal return at or below zero after charges.
The effect only in the bottom liquidity tercile of the universe.
Benjamini-Hochberg across the programme at q = 0.10 does not keep it.

prior.reason: Long-lived globally, some Indian support; our surprise is a price proxy and costs are delivery STT on both sides.

feasibility.reason: Results-date history is not in the archive (#71); event engine (#72).

contamination: Discovery's 527 daily rule trials and the equity library ran on about 2.3 years of daily bars (2024 to 2026) of NIFTY 50 stocks: single-stock timing rules, not this cross-sectional rule. No cross-sectional portfolio has been run on any part of this span in this repo.
